detail: Cross-section of respondents to the 1969 Psychology Today survey (Fair 1978), one row each; Greene (2003) Tab. 22.3-22.6 fit lm, probit, tobit, Poisson, negative binomial and zero-inflated models. No column indexes a unit the rows repeat within.
One row per employee of one US bank (Heij et al. 2004); the page fits multinom(job ~ education + minority) for men. gender and minority are two-level classifications, no cluster.
Cross-section of the May 1985 CPS (Berndt 1991), one row per worker; the page fits lm(log(wage) ~ ...). region, ethnicity, occupation and sector are few-level classifications.
Cross-section of men from the March 1988 CPS (Bierens and Ginther 2001), one row each; the page fits lm and rq wage equations. region (four census regions) is a covariate.
The page (CPSSW.Rd): CPSSW04 is a subset of CPSSW9204, the 2004 college-educated full-time workers aged 25-34.

Repeated cross-section of CPS workers (gender, year, earnings), one row per worker; the source compares earnings per survey year (the page's interaction.plot(year, gender, earnings); Stock and Watson 2007, Table 3.1), so year is a wave analyzed per wave, which is not counted (GSSvocab ruling).
Cross-section of CPS workers aged 21-64 in 2004, one row each; region has four levels, a covariate.
Two CPS cross-sections, 1992 and 2004, one row per worker; year has two levels, a design factor.
Two CPS cross-sections, 1992 and 1998, one row per worker; year has two levels, a design factor. Not a subset of CPSSW9204 (the page).
Cross-section of CPS workers aged 29-30 in 2004, one row each; the page fits lm(earnings ~ education). Similar to, but not a subset of, CPSSW04 (the page).
One weekly series, 1880-1886 (Porter 1983); season is a calendar period of the same series and the page only summarizes.

Cross-section of High School and Beyond students from about 1,100 high schools, one row each, but the table holds no school or county id; unemp, wage and tuition are county and state attributes merged in, and region has two levels.
Cross-section of credit card applicants (Greene 2003, Table F21.4), one row each; lm, Poisson, logit and zero-inflated fits.
Cross-section of an Australian health survey (Cameron and Trivedi 1986), one row per person; lm, Poisson and negative binomial fits.
Cross-section of US electric utilities (Nerlove 1963), one row per firm plus aggregates of commonly owned firms; Greene (2003) Example 7.3 fits a Cobb-Douglas cost function by lm.
One row per paper (Fawcett and Higginson 2012); the page fits glm.nb(othercites ~ I(equations/pages) * pages + journal), journal (three journals) a fixed factor.
Cross-section of married women aged 21-35 from the 1980 US Census (Angrist and Evans 1998), one row each; lm fits.
The page (Fertility.Rd): Fertility2 is a random subset of Fertility with 30,000 observations.
One monthly series, 1950-2000; Stock and Watson fit distributed-lag models with dynlm.

Women from every fourth GSS wave, 1974-2002, one row each; Winkelmann and Boes (2009) fit lm(kids ~ factor(year)) and trend models (Table 1.3), so the wave is fitted fixed and not counted (GSSvocab ruling).
Cross-country cross-section, one row per country (Durlauf and Johnson 1995); lm growth regressions.
Cross-section of Boston mortgage applications (Munnell et al. 1996), one row each; linear probability, probit and logit fits.
Cross-section from the 1996 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, one row per person; region has four levels.
Cross-section of houses sold in Windsor, Canada, in 1987, one row each; lm hedonic fits; prefer is a two-level neighborhood flag.
One row per Massachusetts school district, district and municipality unique per row; Stock and Watson Table 9.2 lm fits.
Cross-section of Medicaid eligibles at two California sites, one row each, with no site column; program has two levels. Poisson, negative binomial and hurdle fits per program (Gurmu 1997).
Cross-section of households choosing fixed or adjustable mortgages (Dhillon et al. 1987); the page only plots, and no column identifies a household or lender.
Cross-section of US states in 1950, one row per state; lm, logit and probit fits (Maddala 2001).
Cross-section of NMES 1987-1988 respondents aged 66 and over, one row each; Poisson, negative binomial, hurdle and zero-inflated fits; region has four levels.
One series of US television rights over Olympic Games; network is the buying network of each game.
Mroz (1987) cross-section of married women, one row each (as carData Mroz, excluded); Greene (2003) and Winkelmann and Boes (2009) fit lm, probit, tobit and selection models.
The page: the 1982 cross-section of PSID7682, subset(PSID7682, year == "1982"), kept as a standalone object.
Cross-section of biochemistry PhD students (Long 1997), one row each; Poisson, negative binomial and zero-inflated fits; prestige is a program score, not a program id.
Cross-section of 32 students (Spencer and Mazzeo 1980), one row each; Greene (2003) Table 21.1 fits a probit.
Cross-section of boat owners surveyed in 23 eastern Texas counties, one row each, with no county column; Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated and hurdle fits of trips.

wide: one row per student, the class type, reading and math scores, lunch, school type, teacher and school-system and school-id columns repeated for kindergarten and grades 1-3 (the page reshapes to long format and fits lm(I(read + math) ~ 0 + grade/star)). The long form of the Project STAR data is in the registry as mlmRev star and rabe_hesketh star1.dta; within each grade, schoolidk to schoolid3 index the schools students share.

Aggregate table of damage incidents per ship type x construction period x operation period cell (McCullagh and Nelder 1989, Table 6.2); Greene (2003) Table 21.20 fits glm(incidents ~ type + construction + operation, family = poisson, offset = log(service)), all three fixed factors with few exhaustive levels.
Cross-section of indoor workers from the National Health Interview Survey, 1991 and 1993, different respondents, one row each; the page only plots.
Cross-section of traders at one trading card show (List 2003), one row each; the page only plots.

Durations of strikes begun in June of each year 1968-1976 (Kennan 1985), one row per strike; uoutput repeats within a year but no column indexes the year. Greene (2003) fits survreg(Surv(duration) ~ uoutput).
Cross-section of the 1981 SOMIPOPS health survey, one row per woman; probit and logit fits (Gerfin 1996).

A single-level conditional logit: travelers x four modes, individual the choice-set identifier; Greene (2003) Table 21.11 fits mlogit(choice ~ gcost + wait + incair) with no random term. Same data as rabe_hesketh travel2.dta, excluded by the same ruling.
One annual US series, 1940-1950; war flags the war years.
One annual US series, 1950-1987; the page only plots.
